## Couple vs. Couple: A Comedy with a Straight Face and Slightly Philosophical Humour

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/para-na-paru-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-05-22 (22 May 2025)
Work: “Couple vs. Couple” is a 2025 film directed by Vladimir Kott.
Tags: comedy, Russian cinema
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/para-na-paru-2025/

In cinemas from today: [*Couple vs. Couple*](https://t.me/kino_voice/595) (*Para na paru*), a comedy with a straight face and slightly philosophical humour

The film turned out deeper and more many-layered than the promotional materials suggest, with their promise of the familiar format of a comedy about a deceived husband and his little trick for love’s sake. In fact we get a hilarious story about the tragedy of Kostya, a desperate literature teacher; this little and at the same time superfluous man is brilliantly played by Dmitry Chebotarev. For the sake of meeting his wife, who is ignoring him hard and has already moved in with a new rich suitor (the comic Alexander Robak), Chebotarev’s hero makes a pass at his student, the daughter of that very suitor, and goes to meet “his girlfriend’s” father at their family estate (given its scale, there is no other word for it).

From there begins the heroes’ long journey towards one another and towards themselves, but the main thing is how it is done! Arguing with a family of connoisseurs of everything material, to whose side his wife has also gone over, Kostya tries to prove the value of the spiritual, the importance of art and feelings, not only of calculation. He endlessly quotes poetry (in Chebotarev’s delivery you could just listen and listen), performs small feats and makes big sacrifices. But at first he beats against it like peas against a wall, against the impenetrable loyalty to everything carnal and physical on the part of the rich masters not only of this huge house but, as it seems at first glance, of life as a whole.

As Vladimir Kott, the director of *Couple vs. Couple*, said at the premiere, a film always turns out a little different from what was originally intended. And I want to add that it is precisely for the sake of this surprise that the film is worth seeing in a cinema (your mood, like the director’s, will definitely lift).

---

## Red Rocket: The Story of a Textbook “Superfluous Man”

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/krasnaya-raketa-2021/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-05-20 (20 May 2025)
Work: “Red Rocket” is a 2021 film directed by Sean Baker.
Tags: drama, American cinema
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/krasnaya-raketa-2021/

On Saturday I went to a cycling festival and rode the whole Garden Ring (Moscow’s inner ring road), and that same evening I watched a film whose protagonist also gets around mainly by bike. Coincidence? I don’t think so

I had kept [*Red Rocket*](https://youtu.be/P0nnJljdryw?si=aBZGEzWPAeW7ih95) in mind for a long time: I liked [*Anora*](https://t.me/kino_voice/243) so much that I wanted to get to know something else from Sean Baker’s filmography. My high expectations were fully justified: the picture turned out to be an impressive, many-layered story of an antihero towards whom you feel completely opposite emotions for all 2 hours. Thanks to the clear division of the stages of the moral fall of Mikey, the protagonist, the film becomes a truly unique emotional attraction that the viewer, willy-nilly, lives through.

By and large, what we have is the story of a textbook “superfluous man” (the classic figure of Russian literature) trying with all his might to make himself. And the main thing Sean Baker emphasises among the reasons for his failure is the closedness of a society bound by norms and unwilling to socialise a former porn actor. It is precisely the silent refusal of any socially approved work that pushes Mikey onto the slippery path we watch for the next 2 hours. And on that slippery path (yes, yes, the one Mikey travels on his bicycle) acquiring the prefix “anti-” to the title “hero” could not be easier. The question of whether the winner takes it all, as the song “The Winner Takes It All” goes, hangs as an ominous pause in the finale. (And, it seems, the answer to it can partly be guessed already in the director’s next film, *Anora*, which continues the same theme of social outcasts).

By the way, do not watch on an empty stomach, buy some doughnuts: you are guaranteed to want them)

## Vermiglio: It Is Not About the Village but About the Women Who Live in It

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/gornaya-nevesta-2024/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-05-13 (13 May 2025)
Work: “Vermiglio” is a 2024 film directed by Maura Delpero.
Tags: drama, European cinema
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/gornaya-nevesta-2024/

The synopsis of [*Vermiglio*](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/film/6038922/) (released in Russia as *Gornaya nevesta*, “The Mountain Bride”; it recently came out on streaming services) puts the emphasis on how a soldier who has fled the war changes the life of a mountain village in Italy. In my opinion, that is not quite right.

As you watch, it becomes clear that it is not about the village but about the women who live in it. Against the background of the decline of the patriarchal family with a man at its head (exactly the kind of family we see throughout the film), the relationships of a mother and her daughters, and of friends and sisters among themselves, come to the fore. The soldier who suddenly appears and disappears serves as a catalyst of character development only for the heroines (all the male characters, it seems, stay as they were). This dramatic circumstance, imperceptible at first glance, sets the film apart favourably from other stories about the home front of the Second World War and makes its concerns unconventional.

Incidentally, another highlight of *Vermiglio* is its visual look. The cinematography is by Mikhail Krichman, Andrey Zvyagintsev’s regular cinematographer and the author of signature cold, detached shots, whether of nature or of characters in close-up. It is pleasing that, despite the chosen style, the finale of *Vermiglio* is nothing like the unambiguous resolutions of *Leviathan* or *Loveless*, which means a fresh cinematic impression is guaranteed.

---

## Death of a Unicorn: An Epic Comedy of the Absurd with a Critique of the Present

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/smert-edinoroga-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-05-06 (6 May 2025)
Work: “Death of a Unicorn” is a 2025 film directed by Alex Scharfman.
Tags: horror, comedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/smert-edinoroga-2025/

Yesterday [*Death of a Unicorn*](https://okko.tv/movie/death-of-a-unicorn) appeared on streaming services: an epic comedy of the absurd with a critique of the present and horror moments.

Despite a stock, sketch-like set-up (a careerist father at odds with his enlightened daughter, though both have been traumatised by a shared loss), the film grows stronger both in script and in ideas with the appearance of the unicorn itself. Besides the horror component familiar from other hits of the A24 studio, *Death of a Unicorn* stands out for the irony in whose atmosphere everything happens. Yes, there are the usual concerns of late capitalism, social inequality and ecological catastrophe, but with a smirk that takes the humour to blackness and complete absurdity. To my taste, such moves let you avoid taking the film too seriously, and therefore think over the problems shown in a calmer format.

Incidentally, the new release is in many ways reminiscent of [*Mickey 17*](https://t.me/kino_voice/522) in its madcap image of the powers that be and other details. In *Death of a Unicorn* at some point it even comes to choosing a kind of “expendables” (exactly [the role](https://t.me/kino_voice/388) Pattinson played in *Mickey 17*). So it turns out to be an unexpected recommendation not only for fans of contemporary horror and social themes but also for lovers of Korean cinema with black humour and a dystopian mood.

## Legends from the Past: Costumes as the Film’s Calling Card

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/legendy-nashikh-predkov-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-04-29 (29 April 2025); updated: 2025-05-01
Work: “Legends from the Past” is a 2025 film directed by Ivan Sosnin.
Tags: Russian cinema, fairy tales
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/legendy-nashikh-predkov-2025/

## 29 April 2025

I am [continuing](https://t.me/kino_voice/538) to tell you about the charms of the film [*Legends from the Past*,](https://youtu.be/uI3T9AGLjOc?si=kAcpej7S-i9jobt4) (*Legendy nashikh predkov*), and the first thing I want to draw attention to, without spoilers for now, is the costumes! It is they, I think, that can be considered one of the film’s calling cards.

I was sincerely impressed by how elaborately the fairy-tale creatures’ appearance is worked out, in particular the shaggy forest Nyulesmurt (Anton Kuznetsov) and the water spirit Shishiga (Natalya Pavlenkova). Given current film trends, they could have drawn in all the complex details of the costumes with graphics and left it at that. But here, and it shows in the photos from the set, every hair on Nyulesmurt is real and three-dimensional (look how in the first photo they are combing his back and at the same time putting on a clawed glove), and every gill and fin on Shishiga is textured and in relief (again, there is even a close-up photo). So the combined effect of the acting and the characters’ appearance is absolutely stunning.

It all looks like a cool continuation of the tradition of the Soviet fairy-tale costume: compare Georgy Millyar in his roles in *Varvara-krasa, dlinnaya kosa* (“Barbara the Fair with the Silken Hair”) and *Morozko* (“Jack Frost”). That Baba Yaga, I think, many people remembered as the model one for life, and again, no graphics: everything rests on the imagination of the costume designers and the actor’s charisma. So *Legends from the Past*, which has all this, is worth seeing)

## 1 May 2025

In cinemas at last from today: [*Legends from the Past*](https://t.me/kino_voice/559), in my view the best contemporary film fairy tale, which has:

- Alexander Yatsenko as a journalist, a father, a keeper of legends and simply a charming bungler
- Characters from folklore unfamiliar to us, that of Udmurtia and Khanty-Mansiysk
- The song “Mesto dlya shaga vperyod” (“Room for a Step Forward”) by the band [Kino](https://zvuk.com/track/55138259) on the soundtrack
- Springtime-beautiful natural locations (and the scenes in town, incidentally, include a lot of writing on the walls of buildings, fences and other elements of the landscape: the town seems to talk to the characters and to us)
- An atmosphere of magic and hope (as in many other films by Ivan Sosnin)

I wrote a little more about this picture [in a piece for Kinopoisk](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/media/news/4011107/), and I declare with full responsibility that it is a must-have of film leisure this weekend.

## From the Life of the ***ed Up: A Set of Sketches on the Absurdity of Social Norms

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/iz-zhizni-nutykh-teatr/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-04-26 (26 April 2025)
Work: “Iz zhizni ***nutykh” is a 2016 stage production directed by Yury Muravitsky.
Tags: theatre
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/iz-zhizni-nutykh-teatr/

Another theatrical off-topic post. While waiting for Alexander Khant’s [*Dzhekpot*](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/film/5266958/?utm_referrer=www.google.com) (“Jackpot”), I decided to go to a production in which he plays one of the leads. The production is called [*Iz zhizni \*\*\*nutykh*,](https://teatrdoc.ru/performances/1253/?afisha_open_widget=1) (“From the Life of the \*\*\*ed Up”), it runs at [Teatr.doc](https://t.me/Theatredoc) (the Moscow documentary theatre) and lives up to its name quite well)

Over an hour or so the viewer gets to see a set of sketches from different moments in the lives of random people: they can take place in a notional café, office, bedroom or station. As a mechanism it roughly resembles *6 kadrov* (“6 Frames”, the Russian sketch-comedy show) or flicking through Reels, only at a slower tempo, in an atmosphere of strict minimalism, light absurdism and an emotionlessness unusual for theatre (which causes no small discomfort)

The thread running through the production is the thought of the absurdity of social norms. It is not done to show concern for strangers, to talk to people you do not know, still less to show intolerance towards someone who annoys you in a public place. In the production the characters (they are the \*\*\*ed up) follow precisely the opposite rules: they poke their noses into other people’s business, try to strike up conversations with strangers and even kick street musicians whose false notes are impossible to listen to. How to interpret what you see is an individual task, but it is definitely impossible to leave the production indifferent.

---

## Lesson: A Teen Drama That Unwinds Its Plot in Reverse

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/urok-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-04-25 (25 April 2025); updated: 2025-06-13
Work: “Lesson” is a 2025 series directed by Sergey Filatov.
Tags: series, drama, Russian cinema, thriller
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/urok-serial/

## 25 April 2025

I had been waiting a long time for the release of [*Lesson*,](https://youtu.be/N8rwCSinSRA?si=ixCXaHvnt_s5QLDq) (*Urok*), and not in vain: the first episode is a success.

Yura Borisov, as a rapper who has lost his career, his money and his girlfriend (literally: she died in a car crash and he survived), is, as always, meaningfully silent and looks on kindly (especially at kittens). Which cannot be said of Daniil Vorobyov’s character: looking at him, I recall a creature from Russian literature called the *nedotykomka*. It is the image of the petty demon sitting inside the protagonist of Fyodor Sologub’s novel *The Petty Demon*. In other words, some small, insidious and clinging nastiness, at first invisible to the eye. Let us see what comes of it in the next episodes, but I have no doubt about how well Daniil Vorobyov’s possessed characters play.

By all the rules of a pilot episode, the teenagers are also getting a storyline of their own, and it is gratifying that it is led by Oleg Savostyuk, an actor who, to my taste, already enjoys credit of trust on a par with Borisov and Vorobyov. It is unusual that after an already thoroughly adult role in [*Give a Show!*](https://t.me/kino_voice/347) (*Dayte shou*) he has returned to school themes, but it is a pleasure to see him on screen in any role. By the way, I hope the line of the not-quite-a-tomcat Igor will develop too; they did not put him on the poster for nothing!

On the minus side: I am getting Vietnam flashbacks from the country house where the teenagers hang out. It is the same location as the fateful party in *Tsikady* (“Cicadas”). Those who know how that series ended will understand my nervous tic.

## 10 May 2025

I continue watching [*Lesson*](https://t.me/kino_voice/550) and cannot fail to note that Yura Borisov and Daniil Vorobyov in the leads are an excellent engine of interest in a series that has turned out not to be quite about their characters’ brotherly relationship.

The story becomes ever more deeply a teen drama: with bullying, emotional dependencies and parental overprotection. And making such a seemingly very typical and familiar set-up interesting is not that easy. The difference is that here the plot unwinds in reverse order: in the first episode, before we properly knew anyone, we witnessed a shooting (which in *Tsikady*, for example, was precisely the final chord), and in the following episodes we get to know each teenager more closely. Thanks to this intrigue there is no obtrusive feeling that everything is heading towards something definite; on the contrary, there is a chance to guess for yourself what awaits the characters.

For now I feel sorry to the point of tears for Mila (the girl more often called Ponchik, “Doughnut”, than by her name), because she is completely blind to the manipulations of Artyom, who exploits her affection 100% (Oleg Savostyuk’s astonishingly vile character; such a transformation sends a chill down your spine). What will come of their joint drug escapades is frightening even to imagine. More darkness is added by the sinister transformation of Kostya (Vorobyov) from a harmless pedantic bore into a maniacally focused scoundrel. The portrait he unwrapped piece by piece over a couple of episodes was obviously the last thread of his fragile psychological stability. Now, it seems, the character’s marbles have come off together with the wrapping paper.

 By the way, where did the pseudo-tomcat with the kittens go? We have not seen Igor for a while, we miss him!

## 17 May 2025

A few words on why the series [*Lesson*](https://t.me/kino_voice/584) has a brilliantly written script.

Initially, because of the given context, we expect Yura Borisov’s character to develop, since he is the most troubled guy here. But in fact his appearance serves only as a catalyst for the transformation of Daniil Vorobyov’s character, who at first looks more stable than a school bell timetable.

Not a bit of it: judging by half the season, Borisov is now playing a consistently good guy who, in essence, finished with his problems before the action began, off screen. Whereas Vorobyov is precisely the one acquiring problems. And the longer his brother is around, the faster he accelerates.

So the script is good precisely for this substitution of what is stereotypically expected of the characters with what is realistically convincing: a pleasant unpredictability of plot arises at once.

## 30 May 2025

The new episode of [*Lesson*](https://t.me/kino_voice/596) in 3 points:

Igoressa is back! At last, if only briefly, we got to enjoy an appearance by this heroine again

The episode’s resolution is not encouraging: for several central characters the remaining episodes risk turning from a teen drama into a crime drama.

Where we were learning to manipulate people, Daniil Vorobyov’s character was teaching. Obviously Konstantin has broken bad, and from here it will only get worse. It is hard even to imagine ways of resolving the accumulated conflicts relatively painlessly for all the innocent.

## 13 June 2025

The finale of [*Lesson*](https://t.me/kino_voice/596) did not disappoint. From the very beginning it was clear that a tragedy would happen, but it was not obvious whom it would touch. It is great that this intrigue remained unpredictable to the end, and when it was revealed, it worked in a very unconventional yet realistic way.

The “superfluous man” in the person of Anton (Borisov) received a resolution classic for 19th-century Russian literature (but it was still unexpected). And Kostya’s (Vorobyov) final monologue definitively fixed the series in the genre of psychological thriller.

I was separately pleased by the scene of giving away Igoressa’s kittens. First, it is as if it were the fate that meeting Anton gave each of the characters. Second, it is the most eco-friendly working through of grief I have seen on film. Zero hints at a second season, an excellent complete story that you even want to rewatch.

---

## The Last of Us, Season 2: The Beauty of Ruins Has Beaten the Dialogue Again

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/the-last-of-us-2-sezon-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-04-20 (20 April 2025); updated: 2025-06-01
Work: “The Last of Us” is a 2023 series directed by Neil Druckmann, Peter Hoar.
Tags: series, post-apocalypse, video game adaptation
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/the-last-of-us-2-sezon-serial/

## 20 April 2025

The opening episode of season 2 of [*The Last of Us*](https://youtu.be/_zHPsmXCjB0?si=j7H8MXia3ZHp2wk2) is simply a combination of the uncombinable.

The first and clearest feeling is that over the 5 years that have passed in the world of the series, Ellie seems to have lost some of her brains. Seriously, this is a character completely incomparable with the first season, and it is not about growing up: vivid displays of teenage rebellion at the age of 19 provoke bewilderment at the very least. Naturally, such a character transformation sets the necessary level of intrigue, but as a viewer I am none the better for it.

Despite Ellie’s wild energy, the whole episode proceeds sluggishly, even for exposition. This creates another dissonance, which, paradoxically, really whets your interest and desire to keep watching. And so, on contrasts, the new chapter of this story begins.

## 27 April 2025

After the expository [first episode](https://t.me/kino_voice/539), *The Last of Us* continued with a brisk invasion of zombies and dramatic changes in the characters’ storylines, which is what we are all here for

The second episode is striking for the lifelike chaos of everything that happens, when before a fateful day people quarrelled by chance, missed each other by chance, and met when it was already too late. However, the overwhelming majority of meetings in this episode bring grief to at least one of those meeting: in this one sees the season’s dominant principle of “man is a wolf to man”. The rest of the season will obviously go on trying to deal with the chain of violence Joel unwittingly set in motion, and exactly what the series’ creators will do with the game’s resolution is doubly interesting.

In my view, the first two episodes should have been released together at once: they make up a harmonious set-up for the season with a variety of storylines ⬅️ But we have what we have, and now, in the third episode, we should expect, I think, a drop in pace. Ellie has a lot to think over, accept and decide for herself before moving on, and in this, incidentally, her situation coincides with that of the whole town, which has just survived a terrible attack by the infected. We wait for flashbacks with Pedro Pascal, place our bets on how quickly the characters will come out of their post-traumatic stupor, and keep watching.

## 4 May 2025

Well, the third episode of *The Last of Us* turned out, as I [expected,](https://t.me/kino_voice/555) to be a sharp drop in pace.

Even the friends’ journey to Seattle is built not so much as a dynamic trip as a meditative drive through the locations transferred from the game to the series. The same can be said of the scene where Ellie looks around Joel’s empty house: in it I see not only a farewell to someone close to her but also a demonstration of the calm, domestic artistic world that remains in the past for the characters.

Nevertheless, the season is approaching its middle, and, given such stretching of the plot, it becomes clear why the series was renewed for a 3rd season)

## 11 May 2025

The second season of *The Last of Us* has passed its midpoint, and it seems that something is about to begin other than the positioning of forces, of which we have already [seen plenty.](https://t.me/kino_voice/576)

Seattle has finally been reached, the girls’ secrets from each other have come out, the enemies and ill-wishers are clear. Before the end of the season I would like to catch at least a glimpse of the meeting with the adversaries and the long-awaited revenge.

There are a couple of questions about the universe. Ellie first, with the confidence of a seasoned reader of specialist literature, tells the psychologist everything she wants to hear from a traumatised girl on the road to recovery. But a couple of episodes later the same Ellie cannot for the life of her figure out what the rainbow symbols on the walls of the abandoned city are?)

Such knowledge of the psychological topics fashionable in our world, unnatural for a post-apocalyptic context, on the one hand, and complete ignorance of cultural symbols from literally 20 years before (in their world), look strange to say the least. On the other hand, such specifics of the screen world are intriguing in their own way and make you keep watching.

## 18 May 2025

The fifth episode of [*The Last of Us* 2](https://t.me/kino_voice/586) is frustrating, and I already regret that HBO stretched the game over 2 seasons.

The beauty of the ruins has beaten the dialogue again, so that even solid suspense loses conviction. Obviously most of the shortcomings are linked to the decision to split the second part of the game into two full seasons: it seems to me this greatly lowered the pace of the narrative and damaged character development.

But there is still hope for the couple of final episodes. First, thanks to the cruelty Ellie demonstrated. In my post on the first episode of the season I [wrote](https://t.me/kino_voice/539) that over the past 5 years Ellie seemed to have lost some of her brains, but now I see that this is more than compensated by determination and principle, as in the good old first season. In the scene of the brutal interrogation of Abby’s comrade-in-arms, I finally found it interesting to watch what was happening, even if the whole scene unfolded in a dark, utterly unpicturesque (unlike the rest of the post-apocalyptic world) corner of a basement.

Second, an impressive line of the hopelessness of people as a species is emerging. In the face of a growing danger of complete extinction (the infection now spreads in the form of spores that poison the air, and the infected are evolving rapidly), humanity continues to splinter into small warring groups, finding reasons purely at the level of principles. Perhaps it would be worth returning to the theme of inventing a cure after all?

Third, a spoiler flashback in the final frames hints that episode 6 may consist entirely of memories. There we will have Pedro Pascal, the unwinding of the plot intrigue and, I hope, gripping dialogue.

## 25 May 2025

In episode 6, *The Last of Us* 2 literally [came alive,](https://t.me/kino_voice/605) and that is encouraging ahead of the final episode.

The whole episode I delighted in the realistic dialogue, the duo of Ellie and Joel and the growing context (it had been lacking until now). But it is obvious that this is a brief breather before the season finale, which is supposed to leave a powerful intrigue hanging while we wait for the next episodes.

By the way, the episode very rarely shows Ellie and Joel in the same frame, apparently to reflect their estrangement before the fateful quarrel. I caught a rare exception for the post.

## 1 June 2025

The final episode of [*The Last of Us* 2](https://t.me/kino_voice/612) is flesh of the flesh of the whole season: ambiguous, debatable and in places infuriating in its illogic.

It is already customary that with Joel’s disappearance from the action, the dialogue sags noticeably. But this episode made me yell at the screen for a different reason. In the scene where Ellie runs into Abby’s comrades and accidentally kills both of them, one particular moment bothered me. The pregnant young woman, dying, asks Ellie to make an incision in her belly and take out the baby, clearly saying where and how to cut. In response Ellie switches on panic (🤷‍♀️), does not even try to do anything (🤦‍♀️) and with a shocked look (as if it were unexpected) watches the young woman die. Let us suppose that is simply Ellie’s character and nothing can be done about it. But in a world where you can be devoured by an infected at any second, the reaction should be up to it. And this scene shows us only how easily the logic of the world collapses for the sake of “complicating” the inner conflict of the heroine, so contradictory, misunderstood by everyone and lonely.

The final cliffhanger with the gunshot does, of course, leave the intrigue hanging, but after the scene described above it no longer impresses so much. It is good that while we wait for the next season we will have a couple of years to think it over.

---

## SWWW: A Crime Drama About Turf Wars in Rostov-on-Don

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/yuzzz-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-04-16 (16 April 2025)
Work: “SWWW” is a 2022 series directed by Stas Ivanov.
Tags: series, crime, Russian cinema
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/yuzzz-serial/

As part of ~~catching up on the basics~~ catching up on important things, I watched the series [*SWWW*](https://youtu.be/kZ1Bk5f28W8?si=SynLIfjFxMlSuGmb) (*YuZZZ*, after the city’s South-West-West-West district), a crime drama about turf wars in the districts of Rostov-on-Don.

- The series has stunning locations: the dangerous aura of Rostov-on-Don is shown unvarnished, with the city’s recognisable southern charisma. And it was *SWWW* that brought the Rostov image (which, in fact, has a rich [history)](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/media/article/4006407/) up to date in the era of streaming.

- Kuzma Kotrelev, Maria Matsel and Anton Kuznetsov created very convincing and three-dimensional characters whose fates you want to think about after watching. Really, these are complex characters; I could not always understand their decisions, but all the more interestingly did the series’ intrigue twist.

- Despite the seeming transparency of the plot about the price of quick money, no triumph of morality is felt at the end. The fate of Rav (Kotrelev) is absurd to the point of hopelessness. And that is probably very right: there is no reason to romanticise the life of drug dealers and assorted gangs, since in reality there will be no lofty finale. In this respect, by the way, the series’ resolution resembles the finale of Sangadzhiev’s *Happy End*, if anyone has seen it.

By the way, are you interested in reading not only about fresh premieres but also about relatively old things? Or perhaps you are catching up on something you missed yourselves?

## About This Very Thing: The Conflict of Idealism and Reality in a Village

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pro-eto-samoe-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-04-15 (15 April 2025); updated: 2025-05-07
Work: “About This Very Thing” is a 2025 series directed by Evgeniy Abyzov.
Tags: series, comedy, Russian cinema
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/pro-eto-samoe-serial/

## 15 April 2025

I am a simple person: I see a project with Denis Vlasenko, I switch it on!

Yesterday saw the start of the series [*About This Very Thing*](https://youtu.be/1uhPwsNq6sE?si=_1eqQkV5FRr_TU_f) (*Pro eto samoe*), about a young sexologist (Vlasenko himself) who, after studying in St Petersburg, returns to his home village and genuinely burns with the desire to help people and teach them to perceive their bodies correctly. But his dear fellow villagers first call him the “willy doctor” and then go as far as beating him up for his unwanted sex education. This is where the main conflict arises, between idealism and reality (senseless and merciless).

TNT/Premier projects (the Russian TV channel and its streaming service) have always done well with village themes (recall *Zhuki*, [“The Beetles”),](https://t.me/kino_voice/373) and with the conflict of “provincial” and “metropolitan” too ([*Telokhraniteli*](https://t.me/kino_voice/430), “The Bodyguards”, will not let me lie). And in this case it all worked out, despite a subject alien to the mass viewer. Besides, Denis Vlasenko works masterfully with images of self-sacrificing young men suffering for their kindness to the world, so the casting is perfect. And the whole theme is pleasantly freshened by a connection, felt subliminally, with Bulgakov’s *A Young Doctor’s Notebook*. Except that in *About This Very Thing* everything is wrapped up in a comic key, but it still stands out favourably against other television projects and makes you wait devotedly for more.

## 7 May 2025

And the recently finished series [*About This Very Thing*](https://t.me/kino_voice/534) surprised with a resolution completely unexpected for its genre

All season Denis Vlasenko’s character seemed to be successfully fighting prejudice about sex education, helping some people, sorting out his personal life; everything was going uphill. And even when things began to fall apart towards the end, I did not expect the finale to be so radical. In short, to avoid spoilers, I will say that after such a last episode it is even pleasant to wait for a second season: they have got me intrigued!)

I hope that if there really is a continuation, it keeps the sweet aesthetic the series’ creators came up with. Its main embodiment is the opening credits, designed as a vivid still with the series’ title in handwriting. I admired them every time.

---

## Hypnosis: A Brisk Start, a Powerful Finale and a Stalling Middle

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/gipnozis-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-04-14 (14 April 2025); updated: 2025-05-23
Work: “Hypnosis” is a 2025 series directed by Timofey Zhalnin.
Tags: series, fantasy, Russian cinema, mystery
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/gipnozis-serial/

## 14 April 2025

After much thought I started [*Hypnosis*](https://youtu.be/pHoWJ67jX5U?si=a8GD2lnx3Fro-1xM) (*Gipnozis*). So far what attracts me is not even the fantasy part but individual features of the alternative reality and the peculiar humour)

The thing is, the series’ three main characters are three friends with superpowers (here they are, left to right): a private detective who can read minds; a lawyer who sees the future; and an Orthodox priest who sees the past. Put them together and you get a real superpower (and basically that is what they do, using one another’s abilities in a neighbourly way).

But how funny it looks in action when the lawyer, needing additional information on some case, asks the priest to drop by the morgue and touch a dead body to learn its past (the ability works only through physical contact). You catch very strong vibes of *O chyom govoryat muzhchiny* (“What Men Talk About”, the Kvartet I comedy), only with superpowers added to the plot, and that is not bad for an urban fantasy like this: you cannot pull everything off on seriousness alone. Indeed, the irony and down-to-earthness of even characters with supernatural abilities help draw the viewer in at times better than a twisty detective line.

## 23 May 2025

*Hypnosis* has finished and made me empathise with the hypnotist maniac. But first things first.

The series has a [brisk, gripping start](https://t.me/kino_voice/531) (plus viral promo that was hard to miss), a powerful finale, but a noticeably stalling middle that spoils the impression a little. Its problem is the intrigue, which evaporates because the viewer knows the moves from every side.

Nevertheless, as soon as the reasons for Piskunov’s villainy became clear, everything fell into place for me. The positive characters turned out not good enough to empathise with, whereas the grief the antagonist went through seems precisely a very weighty argument for revenge 20 years on. It even occurred to me that telling it from his point of view would have been a winning device for creating the story of a raging villain. But even as things stand, the reversal of good and evil made the finale genuinely gripping: what was happening became non-obvious, and there appeared a real rather than illusory choice of the side you want to root for. So to fans of intricate and non-obvious detective stories I recommend it warmly.

By the way, besides all the merits of the resolution, the characters’ reflection in the frame is attractive. A lawyer, a private detective and a priest sit and discuss whether they had the right to do what they did? It is great that the ethical reflection on what is shown is not shifted entirely onto the viewers but finds a place right inside the work: a very metamodernist move. After watching, you want to recall the concept of moral relativism and ask yourself once again about the possibility of absolute evil and absolute good.

---

## Where’s Our Money?: A Gangster Showdown in the Spirit of Guy Ritchie and Tarantino

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/gde-nashi-dengi-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-04-10 (10 April 2025); updated: 2025-04-11
Work: “Where’s Our Money?” is a 2024 film directed by Vladimir Zinkevich.
Tags: Russian cinema, comedy, crime
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/gde-nashi-dengi-2025/

## 10 April 2025

I am admiring the stylish character posters for [*Where’s Our Money?*](https://youtu.be/9IQq9yYgefQ?si=X3Yp1WCyAuzm2L_n) (*Gde nashi dengi?*): from today this luxury can be seen in cinemas!

This is a very brisk, dynamic and simply great gangster showdown in the spirit of Guy Ritchie and Quentin Tarantino, but with allowance made for our context. Despite its modest running time, the film is built very intriguingly in terms of plot and characters, so your attention will be constantly captured by the motley inhabitants of the gangster landscape, each with their own quirk. The humour is top-notch too: it rides on the actors’ charisma, it is purely physical, and there are simply charming absurdities of various kinds. And concentrate when things head towards the finale: everything there is twisted beautifully)

In short, I warmly recommend the new release, and I will definitely rewatch it myself.

## 11 April 2025

By the way, [*Where’s Our Money?*](https://t.me/kino_voice/523) is notable for a couple more things.

First, I found a sweet reference there to *Kuryer* (“The Courier”), a film that, as it were, prefigures the gangster era. Like Ivan in *The Courier*, Kuzma Kotrelev’s character, nicknamed Nauka (“Science”), asks his friends whether they have a dream. The answers drown in the commotion of the plot, but what matters is the question itself, reminding us, as it were, that one should dream “of something great”. Especially in the context of a film focused on profit.

Second, the speech of the characters in *Where’s Our Money?* is real linguistic entertainment. “DelyugA”, with the stress on the “a”, “chikh-pykh” and other euphemisms are very interesting to decode or even to work into your own vocabulary (I confess, I am guilty, I love all these little words myself). And today I was also delighted to discover a [glossary](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/media/article/4010996/) of this slang from director Vladimir Zinkevich and colleagues at Kinopoisk: the perfect cultural plan for a Friday evening.

## Not Like Dad 2: Granddad: A Very Sweet Sequel About a Childhood in the 1990s

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/batya-2-ded-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-04-08 (8 April 2025)
Work: “Not Like Dad 2: Granddad” is a 2025 film directed by Ilya Uchitel.
Tags: Russian cinema, comedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/batya-2-ded-2025/

I have got round to [*Not Like Dad 2: Granddad*](https://youtu.be/69S2gg5qaTM?si=-Dmp2piQFy9FYJZN) (*Batya 2. Ded*), and it turned out to be a very sweet sequel to the story of a childhood in the 1990s.

The rough-edged humour and the buddy movie here are provided by the still-young Andrey Andreev and a radically aged Evgeny Tsyganov. Their duo turned out even more successful than the one with Vdovichenkov in the first film: the strict father-and-son hierarchy in the relationship between grandson and grandfather seems to give way to a more comradely relationship with mutual ribbing and tender attachment. Their whole storyline of holidays in the village goes down in one breath and with a kind smile (which in the first part tended to be crowded out by anxiety over the unstable figure of the father).

I was separately pleased by the line of black-and-white flashbacks from the grandfather’s wartime youth. Some of the camera techniques are borrowed from Urusevsky (the cinematographer of *The Cranes Are Flying*) with his “Dutch angles”, and some of the darkest scenes (in particular, with the labour camp where the grandfather ended up after going through the whole war) are even stylised after Wes Anderson’s symmetry, since we see it through the eyes of a child who imagines his grandfather’s fate in his own way.

The only thing is that, as in the first part, the impression was slightly spoiled for me personally by the scenes from the present day: the grown-up Max’s relationship with his wife is distinguished by neither humour nor originality, and only brings on thoughts that the grass used to be greener and love more sincere (though perhaps this is a deliberately intended effect, heightening the nostalgia)).

---

## Einstein and Margarita: Serebryakov’s Performance and Disappointed Expectations

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/eynshteyn-i-margarita-teatr/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-04-06 (6 April 2025)
Work: “Einstein and Margarita” is a 2022 stage production directed by Alexander Marin.
Tags: theatre
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/eynshteyn-i-margarita-teatr/

A theatrical off-topic post. I went to [*Einstein and Margarita*](https://teatr-estrada.ru/afisha/einstein_margarita) (*Eynshteyn i Margarita*; that very production about Einstein, his lover and their historical responsibility, from which Ksenia Rappoport was recently [removed](https://t.me/oteatre/9260)) and am still under the impression, so I decided to break it down into pluses and minuses:

➕ A stunning performance by Alexei Serebryakov. His acting on stage grips you instantly: Serebryakov not only brings this figure to life but also gives Einstein, whom we picture first of all from the famous photo with his tongue sticking out, a credible depth of personality.

➕ A successful transfer to the stage of Alexander Gelman’s play *Almar* (the name the couple Albert and Margarita went by, from the first parts of their names). They managed to preserve the source’s laconic style, the brisk pace and the sincerity of what happens between two people on stage.

➖ The replacement of Ksenia Rappoport: when I bought the tickets, she was the one listed in the lead, and that was one of the important factors. Note that I have no complaints whatsoever about the acting of Alyona Khmelnitskaya, who took over as Margarita: her heroine is gripping, alive and ambiguous. But my disappointed expectations of seeing a particular actress’s work have not gone anywhere because of that.

## Memoir of a Snail: An Epistolary Novel on Screen

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/memuary-ulitki-2024/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-03-18 (18 March 2025)
Work: “Memoir of a Snail” is a 2024 film directed by Adam Elliot.
Tags: animation, drama
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/memuary-ulitki-2024/

I am just catching up on last year’s nominees: yesterday my choice fell on [*Memoir of a Snail*](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/film/5925061/)

This animated film, unlike *Flow* (the winner in its category), cannot be called soothing. Before us is a rather traumatic story about separated twins, a brother and a sister who lost their family early in life and then dreamed for half their lives of being reunited at least with each other, sharing their misadventures in letters. Of the two, the main heroine is the sister, Grace, but what happens can quite fairly be called an epistolary novel on screen, which is not such a frequent thing in general. The handcrafted style of stop-motion animation is also rather rare: though Adam Elliot, the author of *Memoir*, has already won an Oscar for the short *Harvie Krumpet* in this technique, to my taste the style increases the viewer’s discomfort at what they see. On the other hand, the level of empathy for the characters increases many times over too.

Nevertheless, the film draws you in, because everyone will find something of their own in this diary-like family story. Some will recognise themselves in Grace’s escape from reality (she painstakingly collects everything to do with snails), some, on the contrary, will share the romantic spirit of Gilbert, burning with the dream of becoming a fire-eater, and some will take to the worldly wisdom of the third important heroine, old Pinky, who knows how to treasure the moment.

Personally, at the end of the viewing I wrote down precisely her words:

*Snails never go back the way they came, they always crawl onwards*

---

## Overheard in Rybinsk: Black Humour and Irony Against Nordic Noir

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/podslushano-v-rybinske-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-03-13 (13 March 2025)
Work: “Overheard in Rybinsk” is a 2025 series directed by Pyotr Todorovsky.
Tags: series, mystery, Russian cinema
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/podslushano-v-rybinske-serial/

The real charm of [*Overheard in Rybinsk*](https://t.me/kino_voice/403) (*Podslushano v Rybinske*) is the black humour and irony that keep a twisty, rather gloomy series, even with a touch of mysticism, from turning into a straight-faced Nordic noir, letting it remain a more many-layered work. In which, moreover, the images of the main characters go beyond detective clichés and surprise with unconventional traits.

That is exactly why the shocking finale (I kept expecting Shirmik to amaze us yet again, and it happened) is doubly impressive. It turns out that all this time we were watching the fates of Shirmik and the TV presenter develop in parallel in circumstances that seemingly left no choice. And if the latter rather had no alternatives, though he was not much of a person anyway, Shirmik turned out to be a hostage of his own principles. An excellent transformation by Ruzil Minekaev, it must be said!

Incidentally, the series has an unobtrusive part that gets to the depths of the soul: the soundtrack created by Roman Litvinov (Mujuice), to whose music we have already seen the stories of the characters of [*Mir! Druzhba! Zhvachka!*](https://music.yandex.ru/album/25336347) (“Peace! Friendship! Bubblegum!”) and [*Kapelnik*.](https://music.yandex.ru/album/23531291) (“The Drip”) Only he knows how to combine in sound naivety and a bright hope for the best with the inevitable chthonic murk breaking into our lives from different directions (from our own souls too). It worked 100% and reflected the content of the series exactly: please call on Mujuice to score series more often.

## How to Make Millions Before Grandma Dies: A Charming Dramedy About Fragile Family Ties

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/babushka-na-million-2024/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-03-11 (11 March 2025)
Work: “How to Make Millions Before Grandma Dies” is a 2024 film directed by Pat Boonnitipat.
Tags: drama, Asian cinema
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/babushka-na-million-2024/

Showing in our cinemas is the charming Thai film [*How to Make Millions Before Grandma Dies*](https://youtu.be/HrVX_nHNIUA?si=bSsPgrtRjFRcI3tT) (released in Russia as *Babushka na million*, “A Million-Dollar Grandma”), which has already won the hearts of Asian audiences (there is a whole flash mob in which people show how they cried after watching) and even made the Oscar shortlist for best international feature.

The plot of this dramedy about fragile family ties is quite simple: M, a young streamer who has not quite found his feet, learns that his cousin has inherited their grandfather’s whole house because she looked after the grandfather for a long time before his death. Without thinking twice, M drops in on his grandmother, who, it turns out, has about a year to live because of cancer.

Naturally, on learning of the grandmother’s terminal diagnosis, her children also become active in the queue for the inheritance, trying to get ahead of the grandson. He, meanwhile, in the epicentre of the family struggle, turns out to be the only person truly close to his grandmother (and is himself filled with the best feelings, without any self-interest).

This sweet sentimentality is a great merit of the film, but not its only one.

- First, together with the characters we find ourselves in Thai homes, at the local colourful altars with tea for the gods, in cemeteries where families gather, talk and scatter flower petals over grassy hills. In a word, we see life in a form as exotic to us as can be and in vivid colours, but with very recognisable feelings and experiences: how to earn the love of your family, how to forgive them after disappointments, and what a family even is.

- Second, the grandmother is played by a 78-year-old (!) debutante actress (!!), Usha Seamkhum, and she does it with inimitable charisma, conviction and warmth breaking through the character’s outward grumpiness. Watching her, especially paired with her grandson, is a great and sincere viewing experience.

- Third, despite the seeming predictability of the plot, the film delights with an unexpected resolution, triply touching after everything we have seen in 2 hours. And if you are not afraid of having your heart melted by a wonderful film, this is definitely for you)

---

## Mickey 17: Comparing the Book and the Film, and Pattinson Outweighed Everything

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/mikki-17-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-03-10 (10 March 2025); updated: 2025-04-09
Work: “Mickey 17” is a 2025 film directed by Bong Joon Ho.
Tags: books, science fiction
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/mikki-17-2025/

## 10 March 2025

While [*Mickey 17*](https://youtu.be/tA1s65o_kYM?si=spxE9OVx14Q7_tJh) is on release in the West, I decided to get acquainted with the source and read the novel in the original (luckily, I had prudently brought it back from holiday 🌴, but I also compared it with the [Russian translation](https://ozon.ru/t/xVOlYEb), which does not lose out one bit!).

Edward Ashton’s book is called *Mickey7* and reads as rather compact science fiction: only 300 pages about a man who, in the distant future, signed up for an exploration mission as a so-called expendable, and is now endlessly reborn after dying in various experiments. At the same time the author does not limit himself to brisk action with the protagonist dying, and already in the first chapter puts an ethical question to readers: can the new resurrected version of Mickey be considered the same person who died the day before? Thanks to a mix-up that brings two versions of Mickey together, we get to unravel this dilemma, along the way alternating chapters so varied that the sensation is as pleasant as scrolling a feed of TikToks.

Why have these Mickeys become all of 17 in the film? I suspect the reason lies in the specifics of film language: there you can show Mickey’s various deaths as an attraction (recall how the [posters](https://t.me/kino_voice/388) alone amused everyone), rather than working with the scantier means of text. Besides, the film is directed by Bong Joon Ho, which means the cruelty of all 17 deaths in the style of Korean cinema is guaranteed.

One way or another, I will definitely finish the novel, and afterwards compare how closely Robert Pattinson (lucky man, getting to play immortals!) matches my bookish image of the protagonist)

## 9 April 2025

Well, I have watched [*Mickey 17*](https://t.me/kino_voice/388) digitally and am ready to compare the [book](https://t.me/kino_voice/448) and the text!

On the whole I liked the film, even though it departed from the text, but Robert Pattinson outweighed everything. His performances are carefully thought out, down to the posture and shades of voice of each of the characters; to appreciate it, it is better to watch in the original without dubbing, you will not regret it. The dynamic between Mickey 17 and Mickey 18 was gripping too: this is perhaps the best and most important part of the film, when from the outside you watch literally two parts of a single personality, which the personality must either reconcile or vanish entirely. Just like in life.

It is only a pity that the film mangles one of the most important moments of Mickey’s entry into the “expendable” profession: the task of committing suicide to prove his faith in the regeneration technology by which he will be resurrected. Instead of the real suicide he resolved on in the text, this test turns into a crude shot to his head at the hands of the manager conducting his onboarding. But I understand that in the film this is important for Mickey’s moral portrait, even if it harms the spectacle.

On the whole there is not that much of the bloody attraction one expects from a Korean director here, but there are heaps of social issues. These seemed grotesque: it is clear that the whole part about the local demagogue politician is open satire on Trump. Right down to his supporters’ red caps and the bullet from the crowd that grazed the politician. But this crude local tie to reality is still understandable and, moreover, embellished by Mark Ruffalo’s acting. And for its talented performances the film is definitely worth seeing)

---

## Chemo Romance: A Finale of Mixed Feelings and an Honest Look at Illness

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/mezhdu-nami-khimiya-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-03-09 (9 March 2025); updated: 2025-04-18
Work: “Chemo Romance” is a 2025 series directed by Karina Chuvikova.
Tags: series, drama, Russian cinema
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/mezhdu-nami-khimiya-serial/

## 9 March 2025

As it happens, I started the series [*Chemo Romance*](https://youtu.be/FQjZ9LJUQ_4?si=Sx_q5vAe5rMMuAt8) (*Mezhdu nami khimiya*, “There’s Chemistry Between Us”) while rewatching (and finishing) [*Breaking Bad*](https://youtu.be/HhesaQXLuRY?si=z76qXdtsopEqrPG5) in parallel. The result was a parallel between the male and female views of one and the same plot set-up.

The heroine of *Chemo Romance*, Tanya, works as a taxi driver, is raising two children alone (her husband died), and suddenly learns that she has cancer. Now her main task is ~~to earn money for the rest of her life~~ to find a husband to whom she can leave the children, otherwise they will go to an orphanage.

And if *Breaking Bad* is largely a reflection of the male midlife crisis (only, instead of realising that death is near, the hero literally gets a near death from cancer), *Chemo Romance* is, as they say, just another Tuesday for a woman. Over the first two episodes Sasha Bortich played every shade of despair: at her diagnosis, at a friend’s betrayal, at not quite measuring up to men’s high demands, and at having to tell her children the terrible truth. It seems the whole world has let her down, but there is the ghostly beginning of a new storyline with Nikita Efremov’s character, and that is the best reason to wait for more)

It is great that a series about woman power like this came out for 8 March (International Women’s Day): sincere, ironic, touching to tears, but instilling an important thought: you should think not about death but about life.

## 26 March 2025

I continue watching [*Chemo Romance*](https://t.me/kino_voice/447) and observe two things.

**1️⃣** How differently (and that is great!) Tanya from *Chemo Romance* and Natasha Kustova from *Pochka* (“The Kidney”) fight for their goals. Bortich’s heroine has a truly soft strength, a little naive, vulnerable, held up, you could say, by the viewers’ hopes. Now we rejoice not simply in strong female characters but in their variety (hello to *Outsource* here too)

**2️⃣** How great that Nikita Efremov too got to play such a double role (following the year’s film trend after *Mickey 17*, *Amura*, *Kalimba*, *Vasily* and other projects with twins played by one actor). It only remains to understand whether it is good that, of the two plot options, in which he could have turned out to be a ghost or a living twin of the dead man, they chose the second)

## 3 April 2025

[*Chemo Romance*](https://t.me/kino_voice/494), what are you doing?!

As if Alexandra Bortich’s heroine’s relationship with her children did not already make my eyes well up every episode, they have also decided to move us with music. Specifically, the song [“Ogni goroda”](https://music.yandex.ru/album/36055985) (“City Lights”) performed by Kuzma Kotrelyov and the band Eshchyo Nikak. Maximum respect to the guys for the song (to Kuzma specifically for writing the lyrics), and to the series’ composer Dasha Charusha for the find: it is a stunning scene and an endless repeat for the next couple of days.

Sorry, but in the rivalry between Efremov’s and Kotrelyov’s characters a favourite has sharply begun to emerge.

## 18 April 2025

[*Chemo Romance*](https://t.me/kino_voice/494) is over. The finale left me with mixed feelings (and tears), but first things first)

It is great that Tanya’s choice cannot be predicted to the very last, precisely because the heroine is three-dimensional, and it is not obvious whether she will choose personal, if short, happiness or the long-term relative well-being of her children. The stars of the script aligned so that these incompatible things coincided, but before that there were so many chances to take the wrong turn that the happy resolution turned out to be rather a miracle.

The relatively happy ending looks a little smudged; perhaps the possibility of a second season left open makes it so (I had similar emotions from the finale of the first season of [*Pochka*,](https://t.me/kino_voice/493) which was indeed continued). By the way, if you compare with *Pochka*, Tanya turned out to be no less a manipulator than Natasha Kustova, the only difference being a sense of guilt towards the people deceived) But Efremov’s character, as it turned out, was “glad to be deceived himself” (as Pushkin put it) In my view, Tanya had a great and sincere feeling only with Kotrelev’s character, but it turned out not to be meant to be.

For all the debatable moments of the melodramatic structure of *Chemo Romance*, it has an indisputable advantage. The series shows the situation with the illness honestly and without speculation. The disease is serious, but nobody was planning to keel over and die straight away, because there is therapy. This is a great realistic look at the situation, which is not found everywhere. In *Aktyorishche* (“A Hell of an Actor”), for instance (and this is very disappointing), when the protagonist is found to have multiple sclerosis, everyone simply folds their hands and grieves that in a year he will be in a wheelchair, while the doctors shake their heads, admitting the situation is hopeless. In reality, even for such diseases there is effective treatment. It would be good if all series touching on such serious matters treated the subject as conscientiously as *Chemo Romance*)

---

## The Brutalist: What Is a Question of Aesthetics for the World Is a Question of Ethics for László

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/brutalist-2024/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-03-02 (2 March 2025)
Work: “The Brutalist” is a 2024 film directed by Brady Corbet.
Tags: drama
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/brutalist-2024/

As close to the Oscars as I could, I watched [*The Brutalist*](https://youtu.be/GdRXPAHIEW4?si=fLhACJRsuW6oZAk_), Brady Corbet’s colossal cinematic canvas about a man against the background of global historical events, and vice versa.

Despite some clichés of the “he pursued the American dream” genre, the film has too many silences to fall into that category, and the most terrible scenes (as a rule) remain off screen; viewers are invited time after time to assess only the consequences. This is an interesting move, given that brutalist architecture, no less important a protagonist than, say, László himself, is largely a consequence of the terrible events of the 20th century. Raw concrete as the basis for rebuilding bombed-out cities was a material that was, first, the most practical and, second, the most honest, the one that most concretely embodied traumatic experience. And the fact that Adrien Brody’s character builds his buildings (and his life) precisely in the USA, having fled the European post-war ruins, only helps to focus on his categorical contrast with the whole world. What is a question of aesthetics and beauty for the world is a question of ethics and morality for László. The film reminds us that the horrors of an era tend to end, and their culprits or witnesses to die, but the consequences of what happened will most likely remain before our eyes for a long time to come.

By the way, I want to say something separately about how it is shot and how it sounds. A special technology of film shooting used in the 1950s brings our optics closer to the circumstances of that time: to perceiving history through the means cinema had at its disposal when that history was current. And the soundtrack itself resembles a huge architectural harmony: we encounter repeating themes that stick in your head throughout the film, but we hear them differently, as if finding ourselves in the same place but with different life experience. I think I will even relisten to the film’s score separately (and root for it at the Oscars)

---

## The Summer Will End: The Most Balabanovian Thing I Have Seen Lately

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/konchitsya-leto-2024/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-02-27 (27 February 2025)
Work: “The Summer Will End” is a 2024 film directed by Maxim Arbugaev, Vladimir Munkuev.
Tags: Russian cinema, drama
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/konchitsya-leto-2024/

In cinemas from today: [*The Summer Will End*](https://youtu.be/eorh-gGV7S4?si=Shw7hf_DCy4mCG4A) (*Konchitsya leto*), the most Balabanovian thing I have seen lately (in the spirit of Alexei Balabanov, the director of *Brother*).

Needless to say, the plot about two brothers is eternal, but here it takes a more radical turn than ever. What matters is that Yura Borisov plays the most unstable, slippery and dubious character of his career: it is hard to empathise with him and practically impossible to like him. Though one would think any gangster played by Borisov is a thoroughly comfortable character; we saw that in *Byk* (“The Bull”), *M!D!Zh!* (“Peace! Friendship! Bubblegum!”) and *Silver Skates*. It is great that Borisov can do the opposite too, and for this unaccustomed feeling of anxiety alone the film is worth seeing.

At the same time Borisov’s character undergoes no noticeable transformation, unlike Makar Khlebnikov’s character. His Tima was supposed to grow up, but not the way he counted on (by getting into university in a big city, socialising and building a career), rather through endless psychological traumas from the moment his elder brother returns. The title *The Summer Will End* is about him first and foremost. And though he commits what is perhaps the most shocking act of the film, it is precisely his character who radiates an infectious certainty about what is right and what is not.

By the way, a couple more details go into the Balabanov piggy bank here: the action takes place in Yakutia, an important place for the late Balabanov, and the film also features Alexander Mosin, a regular in bit parts in Balabanov’s films from *Cargo 200* to *Me Too*. For everyone to whom this is close, it is a must-see.

## Prorok: What the Film Is Made Of, from Amadeus to Silver Skates

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/prorok-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-02-24 (24 February 2025)
Work: “Prorok” is a 2025 film directed by Felix Umarov.
Tags: Russian cinema, biopic, musical
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/prorok-2025/

Almost 800 million roubles at the box office: the perfect time to lay out what, as I see it, [*Prorok*](https://t.me/kino_voice/411) (“The Prophet”, the 2025 musical biopic of Alexander Pushkin) is made of)

I have seen this film compared with the most varied musicals and even with *The Master and Margarita*, but I have my own set of film and theatre associations:

- *Amadeus* is the most gripping and dynamic biopic I have seen. Mozart in Miloš Forman’s film wears a pink punk wig, hangs out at carnivals with the atmosphere of modern parties and laughs indecently infectiously. The very example of a classic brought atmospherically to life for millions of contemporary viewers: they assembled a set of conventions associated with the era and details understandable to the modern viewer

- *Marie Antoinette*: Sofia Coppola’s picture is strong first and foremost through the contradiction between image and soundtrack, a kind of audiovisual counterpoint. The young queen of France tucks into pastries and chooses dresses to post-punk, and gets married (with all the 18th-century ceremonial) to The Cure. It recalls the rap numbers in *Prorok*, which at first glance do not fit with the poet’s biography at all, doesn’t it?

- The Gogol Center production *The Misanthrope*: it made this list because of one particular scene. It will not be a spoiler if I say that [one of the verbal skirmishes](https://music.yandex.ru/album/35406151/track/136134537) between Pushkin and Nicholas I is staged as a tennis match. And in the 2018 production one of the scenes with 4 characters was staged the same way, as a contest at once sporting and intellectual. In both cases the effect is stunning

- *Silver Skates* (yes, I compare films with Borisov among themselves, and what are you going to do about it). The living image of the city and its inhabitants with which *Prorok* begins was also shown in a cool, three-dimensional way in *Silver Skates*; it is great that our filmmakers have learned to do this, and for me personally this association promises great impressions from the first frame.
